questions.question: The orbital period of a satellite revolving around Earth depends primarily on:

options.explanation: The mass of the satellite does not primarily affect the orbital period.
The mass of the Earth is the primary factor in determining the orbital period of a satellite.
The radius of the satellite does not primarily affect the orbital period.
The shape of the satellite's orbit does not primarily affect the orbital period.

questions.explanation: The orbital period depends on the mass of the central body (Earth) as per Kepler’s third law, T^2 ∝ r^3 / M.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: Two satellites A and B revolve around Earth in circular orbits of radii R and 4R, respectively. The ratio of their orbital speeds v_A : v_B is:

options.explanation: The orbital speeds are not equal due to the difference in radii.
The orbital speed of satellite A is twice that of satellite B.
The orbital speed of satellite A is not half that of satellite B.
The orbital speed ratio is not 4:1.

questions.explanation: Orbital speed v = √(GM/r). Thus, v_A / v_B = √((4R)/R) = 2/1.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes Kepler’s second law?

options.text: The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis
options.explanation: This is Kepler's third law, not the second law.

options.text: A line joining the planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time
options.explanation: This is the correct description of Kepler's second law.

options.text: All planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus
options.explanation: This is not a correct description of Kepler's second law.

options.text: The gravitational force between two bodies is inversely proportional to the square of the distance
options.explanation: This is Newton's law of universal gravitation, not Kepler's second law.

questions.explanation: Kepler’s second law states that equal areas are swept in equal times (areal velocity is constant).
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: A satellite is revolving in an elliptical orbit around Earth. At which point is its kinetic energy maximum?

options.explanation: The satellite's kinetic energy is maximum at perigee.
The satellite's kinetic energy is not maximum at apogee.

options.text: Any point on the minor axis
options.explanation: The satellite's kinetic energy is not maximum at any point on the minor axis.
The satellite's kinetic energy is not maximum at the center of the ellipse.

questions.explanation: At perigee (closest point), the satellite has maximum speed due to minimum potential energy, hence maximum kinetic energy.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: Assertion (A): The time period of a satellite in a geostationary orbit is 24 hours. Reason (R): Geostationary satellites revolve in the equatorial plane with the same angular speed as Earth’s rotation.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The reason does explain the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: The reason is true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite must have a 24-hour period and revolve in the equatorial plane to match Earth’s rotation.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: The escape velocity from Earth’s surface is approximately 11.2 km/s. If a satellite is launched at this speed, it will:

options.explanation: The satellite will not enter a stable circular orbit at escape velocity.
The satellite will escape Earth's gravity at this speed.
The satellite will not fall back to Earth at escape velocity.
The satellite will not enter a highly elliptical orbit at escape velocity.

questions.explanation: Escape velocity is the minimum speed required to overcome Earth’s gravity entirely.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: A satellite of mass m orbits Earth (mass M) at a distance r from its center. The gravitational potential energy of the satellite is:

options.explanation: The gravitational potential energy is indeed -GMm/r.
The gravitational potential energy is negative, not positive.
The gravitational potential energy is not -GMm/2r.
The gravitational potential energy is not GMm/2r.

questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy (PE) is defined as U = -GMm/r (negative due to attractive force).
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: A planet revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit. At which point does the planet have the highest gravitational potential energy?

options.explanation: The planet's gravitational potential energy is not maximum at perihelion.
The planet's gravitational potential energy is indeed maximum at aphelion.
The planet's gravitational potential energy is not maximum at the focus of the ellipse.

options.text: Any point on the major axis
options.explanation: The planet's gravitational potential energy is not maximum at any point on the major axis.

questions.explanation: At aphelion (farthest point), the planet is farthest from the Sun, so gravitational PE is maximum (least negative).
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: A geostationary satellite is placed at a height h above Earth’s surface. If Earth’s radius is R, the height h is approximately:

options.explanation: The height of a geostationary satellite is not equal to Earth's radius.
The height of a geostationary satellite is indeed approximately 5.6 R.
The height of a geostationary satellite is not 2R.
The height of a geostationary satellite is not 10R.

questions.explanation: For a geostationary orbit, r = 6.6 R, so h = r - R = 5.6 R.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: Two planets A and B have masses in the ratio 1:2 and radii in the ratio 2:1. The ratio of their escape velocities v_A : v_B is:

options.explanation: The escape velocity ratio is not 1:2.
The escape velocity ratio is indeed 1:√2.
The escape velocity ratio is not √2:1.
The escape velocity ratio is not 2:1.

questions.explanation: Escape velocity v = √(2GM/R). Thus, v_A / v_B = √((M_A / R_A) / (M_B / R_B)) = √((1/2)/(2/1)) = 1/√2.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: The time period of a satellite in a circular orbit around Earth depends primarily on:

options.explanation: The mass of the satellite does not affect the orbital period.
The time period T is primarily dependent on the radius r of the orbit as per Kepler's Third Law.
While Earth's mass is involved in the formula, the primary variable affecting the time period is the orbital radius.
Density of the satellite has no impact on the orbital period.

questions.explanation: According to Kepler's Third Law, the orbital period depends on the radius of the orbit, not the mass of the satellite.
questions.hint: Recall Kepler's Third Law: T² ∝ r³.
questions.subject: maha11-physics

questions.question: The gravitational force between two point masses is directly proportional to:

options.text: The square of the distance between them
options.explanation: The force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, not directly proportional.
The force is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the two bodies.
The force is not proportional to the sum of the masses.

options.text: The cube of the distance between them
options.explanation: The force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, not related to the cube.

questions.explanation: According to Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation, the force is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the two bodies.
questions.hint: Recall Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation formula.
